sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy monetization is accelerating, with BELI and BUKA benefiting from rising ad spend and e-commerce transaction volumes independent of global tech sentiment.
Local tech valuations remain supported by domestic liquidity and consumption growth, unlike US peers which face higher rate sensitivity and AI capex digestion risk.
Structural winners are platform and software names (IRSX, CYBR) with recurring revenue, while hardware and telecom equipment (2454, WGSH) face margin compression from input costs and FX volatility.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech names with local revenue exposure (BELI, IRSX, BUKA) as US tech weakness creates relative outperformance; the +0.92% ID vs -1.87% US spread confirms domestic demand resilience. Favor digital advertising and e-commerce enablers over hardware; trim positions in US-linked semis (2454) and telecom equipment (WGSH) on rate-driven de-rating. Maintain normal signal, add on dips to BELI and IRSX for Q3 earnings momentum.

Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally lowering go-to-market costs, enabling smaller brands like KKES and COCO to rapidly gain share from incumbents.
Government social-spending programs and stable inflation underpin rural purchasing power, creating a durable demand floor for consumer staples despite global macro headwinds.
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap consumer names with strong earnings momentum (KKES, COCO, TAPG) as domestic demand holds firm despite global softness; avoid laggards lacking volume growth. Position for Q3 earnings beats and festive-season restocking, prioritizing companies with distribution expansion and margin resilience over broad sector beta.
